priceSnapshot.note: Up 1,546.4 points and 2.00 percent on 24 hours against the 77,307.2 open, and up 1,038.4 points and 1.33 percent against the 77,815.2 morning mark. The morning report's failed breakout has been undone. Its add trigger was a settled 1H close above 78,372.9, deliberately set above the level that had just rejected; the 14:00Z bar closed 78,522.4, clearing it by 149.5 points, and the two bars after it closed 78,575.7 and 78,766.3 without one retrace below the trigger. Price now sits 824.1 points above the 1H EMA200 that capped it this morning and 1,830.1 points above the 1Dutc EMA20. The caveat is in the derivatives tape, not the chart: open interest FELL 0.37 percent across the same move.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 78,029.5, the 1H EMA200, 824.1 points under the mark. This is the average that rejected price twice today - it capped the 78,372.9 spike this morning and was reclaimed on the 13:00Z bar. Two things have to fail for this to print: the 78,372.9 add trigger acted on in this report, and then the average itself. A settled close beneath it means the second reclaim failed the same way the first did, and the 12 to 14 September chop band reasserts into Wednesday's FOMC. Trim the 15.00 USDT tranche added here on that close.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 78,993.9, the 24-hour high, 140.3 points above the mark. Deliberately set at the high rather than under it, because the entire advance from 78,163.9 has been paid for by 642,748 USD of forced short covering and the 78,900 and 79,000 buckets where that covering happened are now spent. A settled close through the high means real bid arrived after the squeeze finished, which is the one thing today's tape has not yet shown, and it opens 79,485.9 and the 79,896.3 11 September spike high.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from HOLD to ADD. The morning report held 35.38 USDT of cash explicitly waiting on its own 78,372.9 gate; that gate has now fired and held for three consecutive settled hourly closes, so the cash is put to work as written rather than re-argued. The reduce level rises 1,006.0 points from 77,023.5 to 78,029.5 and the add level rises 621.0 points from 78,372.9 to 78,993.9; the invalidation stays at 77,023.5, which is now the 1Dutc EMA20 and 1,830.1 points away instead of 791.7.

liquidation.note: 438,650 USD across 77 fills - SHORT liquidations, buy-side, and by a wide margin the largest measured cluster in the window. This is the 78,993.9 push: the covering that produced the last leg of the advance. Read it as spent fuel rather than resting orders, the same way the morning report read the 78,300 cluster that produced its high.

151,367 USD across 20 fills - short liquidations, the deepest point the squeeze reached. Twenty fills for 151,367 USD means larger average tickets than the 78,900 bucket: fewer, bigger shorts were carried out at the top.
52,732 USD across only 3 fills - short liquidations 53.6 points below the mark. Three fills for that size is one or two sizeable positions, not a retail cascade.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull reads up, and the reason to distrust it is in the same data. All 100 fills the feed returned are buy-side short liquidations totalling 642,748 USD, with zero long liquidations anywhere in the 16:19Z to 17:24Z window - a completely one-sided book being emptied upward. But open interest FELL 0.37 percent over the same advance, from 2,169,317,670.01 to 2,161,318,089.08, and funding is only mildly positive at 0.00626 percent per 8 hours, roughly 6.86 percent annualised. Price rising 1,038.4 points while open interest falls is shorts closing, not longs opening. The 13 September midnight session wrote the general form of this: a one-sided flush on falling open interest is an emptied book, which sets up a reversal rather than a continuation. Today that lesson points down, and the 13 September midday session lost money ignoring exactly this caveat after a 704,876 USD short squeeze.

indices.bias: The gap the morning report was waiting on has closed, and that is the read. Morning saw QQQ indicated 703.65 at 08:00 ET, down 1.57 percent, and argued the midday session would likely find it in the cheap zone rather than fair. It opened 703.33, near enough, and has spent the session climbing: 712.57 at 1:47 PM EDT, down only 0.32 percent, with a day's range of 702.74 to 712.46. So the answer is no - the oil-shock gap did not hold, and the mechanical reason is on the macro line, where Brent has fallen from 108.46 at the morning read to 105.74, down 2.51 percent in six hours. Tech that gaps down 1.6 percent on an energy scare and recovers three quarters of it by lunchtime is not repricing, it is absorbing. The zone stays fair, the monthly contribution stays monthly, and the honest lesson is that the morning report was right to wait a session rather than front-run a pre-market print.

indices.bias: The steadier leg, and it has done what a broad index should. VOO opened 697.78 against a 702.56 Friday close, traded a 696.72 to 701.85 range and quotes 701.18 at 1:47 PM EDT, down 0.20 percent - it has recovered essentially all of an oil-driven gap while QQQ recovered three quarters of one. The morning report's argument holds mechanically: a broad fund carries energy inside the index, so a Brent move is partly a revenue line rather than purely a cost line, and that cuts both ways - VOO fell less this morning and is giving back less of the rebound now that Brent is down 2.51 percent from the morning read. The 696.72 intraday low also held above the 696.65 21-session floor by 0.07, which keeps the monthly band intact. Zone stays fair and VOO stays the larger of the two US sleeves.

indices.bias: Still rich, still the one to leave alone, and now with a liquidity caveat worth stating. StockAnalysis reads the Friday close as 104.80 this run, a shade under the 104.81 the morning session recorded, on a plus 2.26 percent session off 102.48 - the largest single-day move of the three by a wide margin and a 90th-percentile print in a 101.15 to 105.23 band. Today it quotes 104.76 at 12:56 PM EDT, down 0.05 percent, on total volume of 583 shares against a day's range of 104.04 to 104.11. A last price 0.65 above the top of the printed day's range on 583 shares is a stale-tape artefact of a thin fund, not a real level, which is its own argument against treating this sleeve as tradable. Buying a 90th-percentile print is the opposite of what a relative-cheapness signal is for. Hold the Japan allocation, skip the discretionary top-up.

calibration.note: The morning 77,023.5 reduce gate did NOT fire and was never close. It required a settled 1H close; the lowest settled close after the 07:04 COT mark was 77,701.7 on the 12:00Z bar, 678.2 points short, and the post-mark low of 77,480.4 held 456.9 points above the level on the wick too. No resting stop was recommended and none was needed. The 78,372.9 add gate DID fire and, unlike this morning's, it HELD: the 14:00Z bar closed 78,522.4, clearing by 149.5 points, and the 15:00Z and 16:00Z bars closed 78,575.7 and 78,766.3 without a single retrace beneath the trigger. That is the specific thing the morning report got right - it refused to re-use midnight's 77,958.5 trigger after that level fired and failed, moved the gate above the rejection instead, and the higher gate is the one that worked. Morning published range with a bullish tilt at 31 bull against 26 bear and price is 1,038.4 points and 1.33 percent higher, so the tilt was correct in direction and understated in size. Discretionary: morning HELD both books and kept 35.38 USDT of cash, which marks the existing 0.00207864 BTC spot position up from 161.75 to 163.91 USDT, roughly plus 2.16 USDT - hence true. The cost of that hold is real and should be named: the same 35.38 USDT deployed at the morning mark would be worth about 35.85 now, so patience cost roughly 0.47 USDT of upside. What morning under-weighted is the same thing this report is careful about - it read the failed breakout as evidence the range would hold, when the 09:00Z rejection was a first attempt rather than a verdict.
